body:
Every language's dependencies have drifted, in some cases by major versions. The `links-notation` spread is the sharpest case because it changes what documents mean, but it is one row in a longer table — the ask here is to bring **all** dependencies in **all four languages** current, and keep them there.

Versions resolved from the registries today.

## Rust — `rust/Cargo.toml`

| dependency | pinned | latest | |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `links-notation` | 0.14.0 | **0.15.0** | |
| `base64` | 0.22 | **0.23.1** | minor |
| `serde_json` (dev) | 1.0.149 | **1.0.151** | |

Also worth revisiting: `edition = "2021"` and `rust-version = "1.70"`.

## JS — `js/package.json`

| dependency | pinned | latest | |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `links-notation` | ^0.11.0 | **0.13.0** | 2 minor behind |
| `@changesets/cli` | ^2.29.7 | **3.0.1** | **major** |
| `eslint` | ^9.38.0 | **10.9.1** | **major** |
| `lint-staged` | ^16.2.6 | **17.4.1** | **major** |
| `jscpd` | ^4.0.5 | **5.0.16** | **major** |
| `eslint-plugin-prettier` | ^5.5.4 | 5.5.6 | |
| `prettier` | ^3.6.2 | 3.9.6 | |
| `eslint-config-prettier` | ^10.1.8 | 10.1.8 | current |
| `husky` | ^9.1.7 | 9.1.7 | current |

## Python — `python/pyproject.toml`

| dependency | pinned | latest | |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `links-notation` | `>=0.11.0,<0.12.0` | **0.15.0** | upper bound **excludes** everything newer |
| `pytest` | >=7.0 | **9.1.1** | 2 majors |
| `pytest-cov` | >=4.0 | **7.1.0** | 3 majors |
| `mypy` | >=1.0 | **2.3.1** | **major** |
| `ruff` | >=0.1.0 | 0.16.5 | |
| `scriv[toml]` | — | 1.8.0 | |
| `setuptools` (build) | >=77.0 | **84.0.0** | |

The floors are so low that a fresh install resolves to whatever is current while CI may pin something years older — the two are not testing the same thing.

## C# — `csharp/`

| dependency | pinned | latest | |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `Link.Foundation.Links.Notation` | 0.13.0 | 0.13.0 | current on NuGet |
| `Microsoft.NET.Test.Sdk` | 17.8.0 | **18.x** | |
| `xunit` | 2.6.6 | **3.x** | **major** |
| `xunit.runner.visualstudio` | 2.5.6 | **3.x** | **major** |
| `coverlet.collector` | 6.0.0 | 6.x | |
| `TargetFramework` | `net8.0` | net10.0 is current LTS-track | |

## The `links-notation` spread specifically

| implementation | pins | 
| --- | --- |
| Rust | 0.14.0 |
| JS | ^0.11.0 |
| Python | >=0.11.0,<0.12.0 |
| C# | 0.13.0 |

Four implementations, four parser versions. The shared fixtures verify that the four codecs agree with each other, but not that they agree about the *grammar underneath*, so this spread is invisible to the conformance suites. link-foundation/links-notation#288 is a live example: whatever is decided about the empty reference lands in a parser release, and today the four would adopt it at four different times. Part of the JS and C# gap is upstream — see link-foundation/links-notation#292, where the JS package is two releases ahead in-tree and unpublished.

## What this issue asks for

1. Update **every dependency in every language** to current, not only `links-notation`.
2. Take the major bumps deliberately — `eslint` 9→10, `lint-staged` 16→17, `@changesets/cli` 2→3, `jscpd` 4→5, `pytest` 7→9, `pytest-cov` 4→7, `mypy` 1→2, `xunit` 2→3 — each may need config or API changes.
3. Raise the Python floors to match what CI actually runs, and widen the `links-notation` ceiling so patch releases are not excluded.
4. Pin the **same** `links-notation` minor in all four, and bump it in one change so the conformance suites always run against one parser version.
5. Add CI that fails when the four pinned `links-notation` versions diverge, and enable automated dependency updates (Dependabot or Renovate) across all four ecosystems so this does not accumulate again.

## Suggested checks

- the shared fixtures still pass in all four languages after the bumps;
- a document written by each implementation reads back identically in the other three;
- the major-version bumps are separate commits, so a regression is bisectable.
title: Update all dependencies in all four languages: major versions behind in each, and four different links-notation pins
